messages:
sam: quick sync: we need a consistent story for hotpath SLA routing + migration strategy before we open the Dedicated beta. Two problems surfaced in canary: (1) noisy neighbor fragmentation after concurrent parallel migrations, (2) surprising quality regressions when routes silently fall back to quant variants.

sam: proposal in short: route-level SLA hints + resident-window tagging. default behavior = route_prefers_resident=false, resident_window_ms=0 (best-effort). routes with `route_prefers_resident=true` get strong residency guarantees (try hard-evict path) and are charged to tenant quota.

maya: Love the resident-window idea. For short-lived chat completions we can set resident_window_ms=5000 so followups hit the full model. That should cut repeated migrate churn.

indra: Important: charging to tenant quota for resident reservations prevents tenants from gaming memory. We should expose `resident_bytes` in the console and enforce a soft cap. Also need a fast path eviction contract: if host pool < 10% free, resident reservations can be preempted in FIFO LRU order.

lee: UX question: how do devs annotate routes? Simple YAML route metadata? e.g.
```yaml
route: /v1/chat
metadata:
  route_prefers_resident: true
  resident_window_ms: 5000
  resident_priority: 50
```
That looks straightforward for infra to parse.

sam: yes. We'll accept route metadata via console + SDK. resident_priority will break ties when memory is tight. Higher number = higher priority.

indra: About the quant fallback quality surprises: we should instrument a per-route A/B probe that samples 1% requests to full-resident model even when serving quant fallback, and compute a lightweight delta metric (embedding distance / task-specific score). If delta exceeds threshold -> auto-disable fallback.

maya: Good control loop. Another protective measure: add a soft_drain window after a parallel migrate completes: mark the quant variant as deprecated for X seconds so cached KV usage stabilizes before we immediately evict. Prevents oscillation.

lee: Concern on fragmentation: parallel migration of many slices causes small leftover slabs. Maybe we should require migrations to align to slab granularity and prefer coalesced allocations. Also consider a background scavenger that consolidates free slots during low-load.

indra: Agree. New invariant: migration allocator must allocate in POWER_OF_TWO slab sizes where possible to minimize fragmentation. We should add telemetry: `alloc.migrate_fragmentation_ratio` and `host.pool.free_coalescable_bytes`.

sam: Ops: default thresholds for canary: host_free_pct_min_parallel = 25, max_parallel_migrations_per_node = 3, resident_preempt_threshold = 10. I'll sketch these in the RFC.

infra-bot: deploy/scheduled canary-migration-policy-v1 to pool canary-07 (rollout: 10% traffic)

maya: I'll follow up with console PR to add the route fields and a short docs blurb. indra, can you add the telemetry dashboards?

indra: On it. I'll include quality delta alarms and fragmentation dashboards.

sam: Cool. I'll update the RFC and add a tiny CLI to set route metadata for temp overrides. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
